title: Storage layout of arrays and linked lists
summary: The same logical sequence can be stored contiguously or linked via pointers across noncontiguous nodes.
description: Both the left and right panels show schematic 5-by-6 memory grids, with rows numbered from top to bottom and columns from left to right, both starting at 1. On the left, the array stores 1, 3, 2, 5, 4 contiguously in the first 5 cells of row 2; on the right, linked list nodes are scattered across the grid, with each node occupying an adjacent value cell and pointer cell.

Light gray cells represent free memory; cells storing the array are green, while in the linked list, value cells are cyan and pointer cells are light blue. The table below lists each node's grid location in linked-list traversal order.

frames.title: Storage layout of arrays and linked lists
frames.explanation: An array expresses sequential order through adjacent memory locations, whereas a linked list is traversed by following next pointers. Consequently, although node 4 lies in the top row, it still comes last in 1 → 3 → 2 → 5 → 4. The figure does not label its specific pointer value. Contiguous storage avoids storing an extra pointer per element; noncontiguous nodes can utilize fragmented free memory, at the cost of storing a pointer alongside each value.
